lesson.title: Beats, notes and chords
lesson.goal: See rhythm as notes placed on beats, pitch as height, harmony as notes stacked together, tempo as how fast the beats pass, and a scale as an ordered run of notes.

say: Each column is one beat and each row is one pitch. Here is C on beat one, then E, then G.
A rest is a beat of silence. The gap on beat four keeps time without a sound.
Play C, E and G together and you get a chord. Hold it for two beats, then land on the high C.
Now play it back at eighty beats per minute. At one hundred sixty, the same beats pass twice as fast.
The C major scale climbs eight notes, one step at a time, from C up to the next C.
